Notes: The model achieved a ROC-AUC of 0.77, meaning it can distinguish between classes to some extent. However, it never predicted prediabetes as the most likely class, giving Recall_1 a value of 0. Since most people belong to class 0, the model tends to favour the majority class.

Class weights helped the model identify more people with prediabetes and diabetes. Recall_1 increased from 0 to 0.304, while Recall_2 increased from 0.174 to 0.598. However, Recall_0 dropped from 0.976 to 0.644. ROC-AUC decreased slightly because class weighting changed the fitted coefficients, which affected how the model ranked its predictions.

Macro-F1 barely changed, moving from 0.427 to 0.428. Most of the new features were combinations of existing columns, so they added little new information. BMI_cat and Age_x_BMI introduced some additional relationships, but they did not lead to a noticeable improvement.

This model achieved a macro-F1 of 0.444, but Recall_1 was only 0.006, meaning it correctly identified very few people with prediabetes. The improvement came mainly from the other classes. Its balanced accuracy was 0.487, lower than E2's 0.515, showing that the higher macro-F1 did not mean better performance across all classes.

Tuning barely changed the results, with macro-F1 increasing from 0.444 to 0.445, while ROC-AUC dropped from 0.754 to 0.749. Recall_1 increased from 0.006 to 0.042, and Recall_2 increased from 0.654 to 0.689, while Recall_0 fell from 0.800 to 0.754. This means tuning shifted predictions away from the healthy class towards both prediabetes and diabetes, although the overall improvement was very small.

Class weights helped the neural network identify more people with prediabetes, raising Recall_1 to 0.243. In an earlier attempt, I noticed that stopping training based on validation loss could select a model too early because the training loss included class weights while the validation loss did not. Using validation macro-F1 for stopping addressed this issue. Validation accuracy also fluctuated because prediabetes examples received much higher weights than examples from the other classes.

This suggests that increasing the model's complexity was not enough to improve predictions using the available features.
